name: Jackson Estuarine Laboratory
use: Estuarine and coastal research lab of the School of Marine Science and Ocean Engineering, on Great Bay at Adams Point, Durham
statusNote: At Adams Point on Great Bay, off the main campus but in Durham

renovations.what: NIST-funded expansion: about 2,150 sq ft addition with two high bays for vessel and buoy work, dive lockers, meeting room and offices, a new entrance, and renovation of 1,084 sq ft of outdated lab space for the Water Quality Lab (grant period Apr 2023–Sep 2026; completion not independently confirmed)

facts.text: Dedicated May 30, 1970, the lab is named for zoology professor C. Floyd Jackson, who founded the Isles of Shoals Marine Laboratory in 1928 and died months before it opened.
It was designed by Pierce and Luykx and built with money from the National Science Foundation and the New England Regional Commission.
UNH leased the Adams Point site from the N.H. Fish and Game Department in 1963.
It was one of the first academic labs in the U.S. devoted solely to estuarine science. Its researchers have trained more than 100 graduate students and published upward of 600 peer-reviewed papers.
Early lab data helped defeat Aristotle Onassis's 1970s plan for an oil refinery on Great Bay.
A $3.77 million NIST grant funds an addition and lab renovation; NIST issued a finding of no significant environmental impact in July 2025.

verdict: A plain 1970 brick lab on a beautiful Great Bay point, one of the first U.S. labs devoted to estuaries; its data helped stop Onassis's refinery.
notes: Addition size conflicts: the grant record says ~2,150 sq ft added, while the old row and a bid listing say ~4,500 sq ft gross on a 2,200 sq ft footprint. Both agree on 1,084 sq ft of lab renovation. HigherGov marks the grant complete, but I found no ribbon-cutting or completion news, so treat the addition as unconfirmed as built. I could not extract the NIST PDF text, so s5 only backs the FONSI's existence and July 2025 date. The old row's contractor (Milestone Engineering & Construction) is unverified and has been dropped. The old UNH Today URL (node/16943) now redirects to the homepage and is not cited. Photos are 2012 exteriors of a modest 1970 brick lab: flat roofs, a dark upper volume, a tall chimney, a superb waterfront site. The setting carries it; the architecture is utilitarian. No interior photos. No public reviews.
judgeNotes: Photo shows a low utilitarian brick box seen across a parking lot. Exterior cut from the old run's 7 to 4: the setting is the asset, not the building. The 2026 NIST addition is marked major, though its completion is unconfirmed.
